newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice makes new contract highs, closes higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice makes new contract highs, closes higher.

text.p: Concern that the El Nino weather pattern will cause a shortfall in Asian rice production, coupled with fund buying, pushed rice prices sharply higher Wednesday, traders said
"We know that there is no room for a shortfall of rice globally in large rice consuming countries, especially in Indonesia, India and Vietnam," said one trader.
All months except July made new contract highs.
In the past, El Nino weather patterns have caused drought or drought-like conditions in some Asian nations and Australia.
Commodity funds were also huge buyers in the rice pit.
Refco bought 400 to 450 lots, and Cargill Investor Services was also a noted buyer, pit traders said.
Gains in September accelerated after buy-stop orders were triggered in the 10.21 to 10.40 cent per cwt range, floor traders said.
Rice closed 17 to 21 cents per cwt higher, with July up 18 at $11.66-1/2 per cwt.
Rice futures volume was estimated at 900 contracts, compared to the 258 traded Tuesday.
